rules.title: Maximum security deposit and upfront charges
rules.quote: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following: (i) rent for the first full month of occupancy; and, (ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month; and, (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.summary: Landlords may not require more than first month's rent, last month's rent, and a security deposit equal to one month's rent at the start of a tenancy.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (security deposit); first + last + security deposit total
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Tenant awarded damages equal to three times the security deposit or balance thereof plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees if lessor fails to comply with deposit, transfer, or return requirements.

rules.title: Security deposit interest requirement
rules.quote: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.
rules.summary: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at 5% per year or the lesser bank rate, paid annually for tenancies of one year or longer.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: If lessor fails to pay interest within 30 days after termination of tenancy, tenant awarded damages equal to three times the amount of interest due, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Security deposit held in separate interest-bearing account
rules.quote: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.
rules.summary: Security deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing bank account in Massachusetts, protected from the landlord's creditors.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply entitles tenant to immediate return of security deposit; lessor forfeits right to retain any portion of deposit.

rules.title: Statement of condition and damage documentation required
rules.quote: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.
rules.summary: Landlords accepting security deposits must provide tenants a written statement of the premises' condition within ten days after the tenancy begins or upon receiving the deposit, whichever is later.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Lessor forfeits right to retain any portion of security deposit or counterclaim for damages in any action by tenant.

rules.title: Security deposit return and deductions
rules.quote: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof; provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following: (i) any unpaid rent or water charges which have not been validly withheld or deducted pursuant to any general or special law (ii) any unpaid increase in real estate taxes which the tenant is obligated to pay pursuant to a tax escalation clause which conforms to the requirements of section fifteen C; and (iii) a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant or any person under the tenant's control or on the premises with the tenant's consent, reasonable wear and tear excluded.
rules.summary: Landlords must return security deposits within 30 days after the tenancy ends and may only deduct for unpaid rent, certain taxes, or actual damage excluding normal wear and tear.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Tenant awarded damages equal to three times the security deposit or balance due plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees if lessor fails to return deposit within 30 days.
